At first the ball seems small, but after a couple of days if you add more air the ball will become large in size. In fact, I had to deflate it some as it became too tall to sit on and I was leaning over my desk. It is common, at least with the balance balls that I have owned, to have a break in period.
You have to allow the material to stretch and soften. This material is made to be flexible and stretch with your body weight. As for the locks on the wheels, they are annoying, but I do understand their purpose. I used some twisty ties to tie them up until I wish to use them. So far they have not come down.
All in all this is a great chair, especially if you like to wiggle on a balance ball instead of being stationary. I find myself moving around from side to side and bouncing every so slightly the whole time I am sitting on it, except while I am typing.
If you are they fidgeting type of person, this chair will make you very happy.
I did buy the cover by Gaiam that is velvety and it is a little large for this ball, but I was able to make adjustments to the cover and it looks great on the chair.

text_fidelity_a: MOPAL ABLE-T Gyro Ball, NO PULLSTRING Needed, endorsed by a Certified Occupational Therapist (OTR/L)… I am retired, but the majority of my working life was spent working on a computer.  I have arthritis in my hands, wrists and while it could be the same in my shoulder, I believe the pain there is from carpal tunnel syndrome due to years of typing hour after hour on a computer. I tried this ball to see if it would assist in building up a bit of strength in my arms and to see if it could dissipate a bit of the pain in both my wrists and shoulders.  It did take me a few failed attempts to figure out how to use this ball, but once I got what I needed to do to keep the ball moving I could feel the benefits.  Well, maybe not while I was holding the ball and moving my hand/arm around, but after I stopped on my right (dominant) side, I could feel my shoulder kinda tingly, but no immediate pain like it usually feels when I stretch or move that area.  I am going to keep using this ball every day and hope that it truly makes some permanent changes to how my shoulders feel. text_fidelity_a:
FINIS Swimp3 1GB Waterproof MP3 Player I bought this primarily to listen to Podcasts and some music while swimming laps. When it arrived, I was pleased with the hardware quality and ease of use. I loaded up some music and Podcasts and headed for the pool. It was relatively easy to clip the units to my goggles. The controls could be better, but are not terrible. I put it on, started playing a Podcast, put in my earplugs and started swimming. I had been concerned that my goggles might leak or come off during turns with these units clipped on, but it was not a problem at all.
The problem, though, was the sound. If sitting perfectly still underwater, it sounds decent. Pretty much on par with my 30-year-old one-speaker clock radio. However, even with earplugs, the noise of swimming and rushing water overpowers it. If I play familiar songs I can tell what I am listening to and somewhat enjoy them. However, forget about the spoken word. I had to turn the volume up really loud to be able to make out most of what was said on the Podcast due to distortion and background noise. And then it was just too loud to be enjoyable. In fact, I am sure that others in the pool could hear some sound from it. I tried to adjust it in every possible way, and followed the instructions precisely.
This seems like a good idea, but I am disappointed, especially for the cost.

Pros: Solid design, no earphones or earbuds, can still wear earplugs, easy to wear, stays on goggles and doesn't pull them off, easy to load songs.
Cons: Price, 1 GB of storage is a total insult, limited features and controls for an MP3 player, poor sound quality overshadows all else.
text_fidelity_b: FINIS Swimp3 1GB Waterproof MP3 Player

The Bowflex dumbbells have lasted me over a decade and they have worked great. They cost many hundreds of dollars, since they did not have much competition when they came out.

These dumbbells are 25 pounds maximum, versus the 52 pounds of the Bowflex. Most men need more than 25 pounds for gaining muscle, and even 52 pounds is light when doing leg exercises. Many exercises are enhanced with a lighter weight.

The actual weight I measure is 25.5 pounds, and every lower weight selection is a little bit higher than the target weight. The weight discs are made of metal. Bowflex coated theirs in plastic to make them less damaging if dropped.

This product is easier and quicker to use than the Bowflex. The ratcheting mechanism it uses seems superior in terms of simplicity. I question how long it will last and would be worried about it failing while exercising. This product is three inches shorter than the Bowflex, which is good since the long length of the Bowflex is a negative. These are quieter when being used than the Bowflex.

The current price is $90 for one. The current Bowflex price is $200 for one. I really like the Bowflex stand. One of the main benefits of the stand is that you are at less risk of hurting your back. Since these weights are only 25.5 pounds, the risk to your back is inherently less.

Compared to individual weights, or ones where you have to screw off the end caps to add plates, this type of dumbbell is a good investment. If you can afford them, the Bowflex dumbbells are great.

text_fidelity_a:
Optimus - Hiker Plus Single Unit The only reason this stove did not get a five star rating is because it arrived in a sealed box almost fully disassembled. None of the screws or twist on fittings were still attached. The tank pivot screws were both loose inside as were the tank and heat shield floating around in the box. The tank cap was also loose as was the pump collar. In addition a lot of these have faulty NRVs (None Reverse Valves) whihc keep pressure from the tank backing into the pump and either leaking fuel or pushing the pump plunger back out after you have pumped it up. I would have thought a conscientious seller would hear all the little parts rattling around inside and done something.

This is both an engineering flaw and assembly failure to not have these things tight enough to make it to the customer. It took some time to assemble it properly as the parts diagram doesn't have enough detail to tell what order things went under the tank pivots. You have to search the internet and find what was next to the tank, bracket and shield arms. Then you MUST USE THREAD LOCK to keep this from happening again as the screws are too short and don't bottom out before being tight. When the tank is slid in and out of the stove it turns the screws and eventually they will come loose again. They should have used shoulder screws or longer screws like on previous models, then they could be fully tightened and left that way. Once it was properly assembled and the threads on the tank pivots locked and the NRV removed, repaired and replaced and properly tightened, all was good with the world.

Now to the stove. This is NOT a backpacking stove. It is a brick! You would think with the name "Hiker" it would be pretty light like the Svea 123 which is a little miracle, but not. However it is indestructible when properly assembled. The burner is very hot and also pretty noisy. The pot supports are widely spaced but most pots will fit without a problem. The stove has no feet, just the flat bottom of the case. You may need to use little rocks/sticks to keep it from wobbling.

Now to it's use. First it can use several fuels but not with equal ease. Choices are Naphtha (Coleman White Gas Fuel), Kerosene 1K, Diesel or if you have some laying around Jet Fuel, which is somewhat like Kerosene.

There is a bit more of a trick to lighting it without losing your eyebrows or hair for that matter. Until you get blue flame you have to meter the throttle often. First pump it up until you start to feel increased resistance, about 20 - 50 strokes. The plunger does not stay in after the last stroke like Coleman appliances. It works it's way back out about half way. That is normal. Now hold a flame to the bottom of the burner FIRST if you can and open the throttle until it lights then turn it back down and wait. Either the flame will start to die after a bit or you will start hearing the hissing of the stove starting to generate. Either way start opening the valve slowly again and let it create a flame about 6 inches high but not higher or the fuel can start running all over the bottom of the case and you will have a bonfire. As the flame starts hissing and turning blue you can start opening the valve more and more until you have a constant blue roaring flame. You are good to go now. You will need to add a few pumps as the flame goes down now and then.

When you are done close the valve and let the whole thing cool a few minutes, them push the pump in and slide the tank in. Drop the valve knob inside and snap the lid closed. If is going to sit more than a few months drain it.

Fuels: Although it will burn all listed, some work better than others. Also outside temperature has an effect on each fuel's performance. White gas is fastest to light and Diesel for fastest boil. Kerosene is a good middle point. Diesel.takes a LOOOOOOONG time to light. I didn't have any Jet A. Remember when changing fuels to drain the old fuel well and give it a quick rinse and drain with a couple ounces of the new fuel before filling.

Here are some fuel comparisons I made on a 90 degree day:

Fuel - Light time to max - Boil time for 2C tap water from tap temp
White Gas - 1 1/2 minutes - 3:15 minutes/seconds
Kerosene/Klean Heat* - 3 minutes and can bee sooty - 2:30 minutes/seconds
Diesel - 5 minutes ** - 2 minutes

* Klean Heat is a "Klean Strip" brand odorless Kerosene substitute. I like it for indoor wick lanterns as it gives off much less odor and is very clean burning. However in pressure stoves I don't see a difference in either odor or performance.

** I could not get the Diesel to burn a full blue flame. There were always yellow tips and it was not fully efficient as evidenced by the soot on the bottom of the pot. This is the only fuel which did this. I checked with the manufacturer and they said this is normal as Diesel is the dirtiest fuel. They recommended white gas as having the least problems and maintenance in the long run.

Enjoy your rugged little gas stove. It should last you a lifetime and still have life in it with proper maintenance.
text_fidelity_b: Optimus - Hiker Plus Single Unit

It's insulated and keeps your water somewhat cool,but on a hot day the water gets warm. You can slide a soft flat ice pack in the pack on the back part on the inside of the pack.  That has helped to keep my water cool.  It has many pockets.  Enough to hold a sandwich, extra drink bottle and a small first aid kit. There is also a zipper pocket on the front for smaller items like a wallet, keys, tissues,etc. It also has 2 wrap around stomach and chest straps so it doesn't slide around and cause irritation on your back and shoulders.  Shoulder straps are padded and stay secure when adjusted. Holds 2 and a half 16oz water bottles poured into the water pack.  This is usually enough for me on a 5-7 mile hike.  I also put 2 extra water bottles in the backpack part of the bag. Just in case I need them. I purchased the khaki one with the American flag on it.  I chose the color because it is light and wouldn't get too hot in the sun, black or a darker color would. The water tube mouth piece takes a little getting used to as far as figuring out how to get the water to flow easily into your mouth but it's not too bad after you get it down. There is also a protective foam over the water tube from the bag to the end of the tube. The mouthpiece has a cap cover which stays attached with a piece of plastic so you can't drop the cover. Overall I think it is a great water backpack with plenty of room for a day hike.

text_fidelity_a:
Marcy Folding Motorized Treadmill/Electric Running Machine - Easy Assembly JX-650W So this is a rather nice basic treadmill (well by today's standards), that comes in a relatively compact (like fits in a minivan compact) box that's crazy heavy. Mine arrived in good shape, though the box had some battle scars and FedEx kinda locked us in by pupping the box so the door wouldn't open. The console and electronics would have been top notch 10-15 years ago, but it's not some web connected device with monthly subscriptions to live trainers ... then again, you don't pay for all that either. When not in use, it folds up, and gives you space for stretching or whatever.

The running platform is comfy, wide, and able to handle longer sessions. It could use better handrails (they're small, yet always in the way--I guess it helps you keep your form), and treadmills that cost twice the price are better made... then again, this isn't twice the price. The belt stays firm up to 6mph, where it starts to slip. That's enough for a walk, jog, and some running. At 7mph the belt starts to slip forward (only slightly) with each landing. Serious runners (and arm swingers--those handles can hurt!) may want to look elsewhere.

The only other nit to pick is a short cord (nothing a good extension cord couldn't remedy).

It all comes down to needs and cost. If you need or really want more, well this isn't for you. If you're looking to walk before you run (so to speak), this is for you. The price is right, it's built to last, and if you outgrow it, you could recoup much of the cost.

I'll update the review as needed, but I'm very happy.
text_fidelity_b: Marcy Folding Motorized Treadmill/Electric Running Machine - Easy Assembly JX-650W

CASEMATIX Hat Travel Case for up to 4 Baseball Caps with Crush-Resistant Hard Shell Outer, Adjustable Shoulder Strap and Comfortable Handle - Portable Hat Case Carrier for Travel and Hats Storage My wife and I recently traveled and I wanted to take along more than one hat, but the case I have that is very similar to this on holds 6+ hats and therefore a larger case. It didn’t fit. But when our stuff was packed I thought if I’d had a smaller one, I could have taken it with and packed it, rather than carrying it separately. I saw this CASEMATIX Hat Travel Case for up to 4 Baseball Caps and was certain it would have fit perfectly into the suitcase. I hate the idea of the case going outside - it’s “small” and things get lost that way. Not to mention, can be easy for someone to grab and walk away... or lost...

So I grabbed this CASEMATIX Hat Travel Case for up to 4 Baseball Caps as an alternative to my larger version. That one is good and I like it - for the car, for storage, for keeping them nice. But this CASEMATIX Hat Travel Case for up to 4 Baseball Caps has a few bonuses that add to it.

1. It’s a nice size and I do feel confident it’ll pack well - depending on the trip and size of the suitcase - but that I would be able to get it into our bags one way or another - and allow me more than one hat. I also don’t like hats laying around when we are gone - in the car, a hotel room - where prying eyes might be tempted. So this is a good size for having a few choices, and ease of carry.

2. I like the air holes. Honestly, I can’t remember if the other has them, but when I saw them on this one I was thrilled. Not that my hats are smelly, and I keep them out most of the time (for airing out) and if I do sweat in them, let them dry before stacking. But the air holes mean they are not sitting in something heating, holding sweat I missed or didn’t have time to dry, that kind of thing.

3. There is a bump in there! I tried to show in the various angles of the photos, but there is a “bump” built into the bottom - outside it looks like a divot up into the case - so that you can fold up the back of the hat and rest it on here, giving the hat support, and the others on top also have that support. It’s a great addition. It means they are not smashing down on one another and can better hold the shape. Love this idea.

4. The size seems perfect. The other one I have holds more, and I do need that from time to time. But this one is a perfect size for up to 4 hats and that means I can have a nice, but not overly obnoxious choice of hats when we travel. And while I have not gotten the suitcase back down since this has arrived I have every confidence in my packing skills (mom was a flight attendant) that I will be able to get this CASEMATIX Hat Travel Case for up to 4 Baseball Caps into the suitcase and keep it out of sight and without fear of loosing it. I do not believe it would go into a carry on - if you’re thinking for a flight - but a little bit larger bag may do.

In the end this CASEMATIX Hat Travel Case for up to 4 Baseball Caps is a nice addition to our travel gear - be it day trips, weekender, or full on vacation. I’m happy with the design and build, the materials seem solid, and I like how it holds the hats - there is room for them on top so as not to smash down when closed as well. It protects them - I am all about taking care of my stuff - and allows me the freedom to have options while we are out and about. I’m very happy with this CASEMATIX Hat Travel Case for up to 4 Baseball Caps.

text_fidelity_a:
Sportsroyals Stair Stepper with Resistance Band and Vertical Climber Exercise Machine for Home, More Than 300lbs Weight Capacity I had a stepper back in the 90s that I liked and used often, but it grew tight, hard to step (they tightened), and I ended up dumping it after only a few months. I wasn’t sure I’d ever get another stepper because of this, but as I’m trying to get in exercise even when I can’t always do the things I normally do. But would this be worth it - and why is with that “side to side” movement?

1. It arrives almost completely assembled, with only the handles needing to be hooked on and the readout box mounted.
2. The mounting of the box is easy - hook onto the attached cord, then place it onto the mount.
3. The handles are easily attached with carbeaner hooks.
4. You’re ready to go!
5. The platforms for your feet are large, wide, and should fit most foot/shoe sizes. There are “ridges or ripples” to the surface; they are not ‘hard,’ but rather produce a good traction surface. I am standing on them and did 100 steps in bare feet to see how comfortable and I was fine. Could have kept going. In shoes they are equally comfortable and keep my feet (with/without shoes) from slipping.
6. The handles and bungee are great for added effort. I’ll usually keep them in my hands throughout the workout, altering using/not using them, changing the direction I’m pulling in in order to give my arms various things to do. They provide a solid workout, giving my arms a nice burn to compliment the work my legs are going.
7. THE STEPPING... I was worried about the side to side movement of the stepping - I’ve never seen or experienced this before. I LOVE it! In the past I’ve had issues with my hips and knees from stepping - or treadmills - but I find this movement is very natural and for some reason does not cause me pain. I recently tore my hamstring, but I’ve hit a point in recovery where I’ve been on the stepper every day for a week and I’ve felt great - it’s actually worked some minor knee pain I’ve been having WHILE stepping. This is a great movement and I’m thrilled it’s part of the design.
8. So far the stepping is very smooth - I feel like the system used to create the movement is superior to the steppers I had in the 90s. This leads me to think it’ll last far longer than that stepper system. If it does, this will be a perfect unit for me.
9. It’s a great height, sturdy, and strong. Okay, it’s heavy - but it should be. It has to hold you up and in place - and it does. It’s height is nice - I can stand at my conversion standup/sit down desk and work. And it’s strong enough to make me feel safe and secure.

Overall this is a great unit and I’m thrilled with it. I’ve been at it a week and feel like it’s becoming a regular part of my workouts. I’m happy to recommend this stepper.
text_fidelity_b: Sportsroyals Stair Stepper with Resistance Band and Vertical Climber Exercise Machine for Home, More Than 300lbs Weight Capacity

text_fidelity_a:
Xiaomi Fitness Tracker, Mi Band 3 Heart Rate Monitor Activity Tracker Watch 50M Waterproof Smart Bracelet 0.78 OLED Display Weather Forecast Wristband Pedometer Calories Burned Sleep Monitor Black My new job requires me to wear a watch and at the same time I joined a gym so rather than a regular watch I opted for an inexpensive fitness band. (I once had a FitBit. Didn't like it so I returned it and vowed never to buy another health monitoring wristband. Any device that counts waving and typing as step counts is too sensitive, therefore inaccurate and useless. Why spend the money only to be one of the cool kids!?!?)

I went into this with a bit of a negative attitude. But given the price even if all it did was tell time I'd be content. Wow! It is good to be wrong!! I have worn this constantly for 2 months resulting in the following review.

Once it paired with my Samsung Galaxy I was impressed with the size and brightness of the clock display. Then came the fun stuff. Setting up for local weather; current, tomorrow, and next day and it's always accurate.

Caller ID, texts, email and incoming calls notifications are a higher intensity vibration than others I've tried. I have always felt the Mi Band 3 vibration regardless of what I'm doing. I really like this while my phone is muted so I remember to check it later. I can also read the shorter messages if my phone is out of reach.

I can't vouch for degree of waterproofing but it's certainly shower and dish washing proof which is good since the Xiaomi Mi Band is lightweight and very comfortable so I often forget I'm wearing it.

I like that I can set it when I go to the gym and get a reading on steps, distance, heart rate, etc. This becomes a subset of the daily activity record.

The sedentary reminder is helpful when I'm ‘in the zone’ while working on a project. I'm not convinced the heart rate is accurate but I suspect it's fairly close for those if us not needing a medical reason to monitor our heart. I don't believe much of anything the Sleep Monitor says but then I don't care about that either.

The battery life is at least 2 weeks. I've only charged mine 3 times in 2 months.

Nothing is perfect, including this Mi Band 3. Navigating through the myriad of settings can be frustrating. There is definitely a learning curve when trying to figure out how to see a specific option : Swipe up? Swipe down? Swipe to the side? Which side?

The other issue is when it changes to military time or suddenly jumps an hour or two ahead/behind for no reason. It took me awhile to find the fix for these problems. Shut down Bluetooth and turn off phone for a minute or two. Turn phone back on, turn on Bluetooth and after about a minute everything should go back to the way you had it originally. I've only had each of these problems happen once.

I am very impressed with the Mi Band 3. And the options can't be beat, especially for the price. This would be a good starter fitness band for a kid or someone just wanting to see if a fitness band is useful to have.
text_fidelity_b: Xiaomi Fitness Tracker, Mi Band 3 Heart Rate Monitor Activity Tracker Watch 50M Waterproof Smart Bracelet 0.78 OLED Display Weather Forecast Wristband Pedometer Calories Burned Sleep Monitor Black

text_fidelity_a:
OxGord Live Animal Trap - Humane Catch & Release Large 32" Cage Best for Wild Animals, O-Possum, Stray Cat, Rabbit, Rodents - No-Kill Bait Trapping Kit - Heavy Duty, 2-Door, Foldable 32" X 12" X 12" This is my first use of a trap -- used for cats in NE suburban backyard. Pretty good product: caught 5 cats, 2 possums and 1 raccoon in a couple of months over this winter. There were 3 escapees.
Some suggestions:
The trap I received was an entirely wire grid device. Older photos show a solid sheet metal closing door.
Several of the clips from critical places had not been installed and were rattling about in the box. In particular, one of two clips that holds the
trap door to the roof of the trap had to be installed or substituted for with wire. These clips are not the sturdiest. One escapee pulled one loose.
I found that it took some practice to set the trap to have a just so sensitivity, and a little bending of the spring catch. It's not complicated, but plan on practicing. Furthermore, desperate animals will dig up enough soil to cover many important joints, so there is need for cleaning and oiling to keep the mechanism working properly. Snow or soil underneath the trap lever will prevent closure.
I also found that the rear door closure with a large clip and a metal rod is not adequate. A small, determined animal can escape. I simply added a piece of telephone wire to hold the rear door to the roof of the trap securely.
text_fidelity_b: OxGord Live Animal Trap - Humane Catch & Release Large 32" Cage Best for Wild Animals, O-Possum, Stray Cat, Rabbit, Rodents - No-Kill Bait Trapping Kit - Heavy Duty, 2-Door, Foldable 32" X 12" X 12"

text_fidelity_a:
Therm-a-Rest Z Lite Sol Camping and Backpacking Sleeping Pad I've backpacked with this three times now and I've had good experiences with it. That said, it has major advantages and disadvantages, so you'll need to know how this fits into your camping/backpacking situation:

Pros:
- it's insanely light
- it will keep you warm from the cold ground
- it's incapable of being punctured (it's foam) so no need to worry about mid-trip repairs regarding rips

Cons:
- it is not cushy/comfortable. If you need comfort, this is not it. It's designed for weight and heat retention, not comfort
- volume. takes up more space than an inflatable mattress pad. If you have a way to strap it outside of your back this probably isn't an issue

That is all. If you're a deep sleeper and you're doing a long, ultralight trip, this is a good option. If you need more comfort and are less concerned about weight, you may want to invest in a good inflatable mattress pad

text_fidelity_a:
NCAA North Carolina Tar Heels Can Cooler, 16 I have this exact same cooler from another team, and got this one as a gift for my cousin, who is a huge fan. This cooler is incredibly well-made and I'm thrilled that I got it! (I ended up buying everyone their favorite team's cooler in this same brand, and they were a huge hit over the holidays!)

The first great surprise when it arrived was that it is made by Coleman, with tags on it to prove it. Coleman doesn't make bad stuff, in fact, they have a long history of well-made products, so that was a really nice bonus.

On top of that, there are all kinds of quality extras built into it. For example, when you lift the lid, there is a mesh ice-pack holder built right into the top of it. On the outside of it, there are mesh holders on each side (I use them for napkins, straws, or nutrition bars). Then in the front there is a nice zippered compartment that you can securely stash a few things in. The zippers are high quality and the materials, inside and out, are high quality as well. The strap is wide, strong and adjustable. Another nice perk is that it has a little pad where the strap will go over the shoulder, which really makes carrying it much more comfortable. The cooler holds a lot, and really does a great job at keeping things nice and cold. I just put my ice packs in it with our bottles, sandwiches, etc., and we are good to go.

I also got one of these coolers for a friend who is disabled and likes to keep a cooler next to her bed. Well, she'd gotten fed up with coolers that didn't keep things cold for very long and she had switched to using a spaghetti pot (for real!) with ice packs in it, to keep her ginger ale chilled, for constant nausea. She said that with a few frozen ice packs in it, she actually can go two whole days without having to replace the ice packs. She also said it fits great on her scooter when she's on the go.

Made by Coleman, like I said, and with lots of nice features, this high quality cooler is a must-have and a great gift. Check out the same cooler with other team logos. Just make sure you get the one like this one from "TLG8," to get the high quality one I just described. Thanks for reading my review. Hope it helped someone.
text_fidelity_b: NCAA North Carolina Tar Heels Can Cooler, 16

Lifetime Crank Adjust In Ground Basketball Tempered Glass Backboard I'm an aging man who still likes to shoot some hoops, so my rim hanging days and blocking shots off the backboard days are over. That being said, I haven't used a nicer hoot outside of a gym (and even then they often aren't this nice). It's all glass and steel, and while 54" is a bit smaller than an official 60" backboard, it's common for outdoors and doesn't offer any real limitations (and after lifting the 160lb box for this, I couldn't imagine how much a 60" box would have weighed!). It's also a 4" pole, which is less than some other models that have 5" or 6" poles. If Lebron were coming over to jam, I would definitely want the extra build, but 4" is fine for me (used to be all you saw).

Delivery was prompt (Amazon used a local delivery company with a box truck/dolly who called ahead to arrange for delivery and brought all the way inside my home. Installation was relatively easy, but this time of year it depends as much on weather and limited daylight hours as anything. The result is solid, and it's easy to dial the height in just right. I don't adjust the height for anything else, but a younger version of myself would lower to allow for some likely sad looking jams.

I recommend this unit for most folks. The compromises with the 4" pole and 54" board really don't see you losing much.
text_fidelity_b: Lifetime Crank Adjust In Ground Basketball Tempered Glass Backboard

Crosman American Classic Pump Air Pistol (.177) Back in 1977 I purchased one of the first models of this pistol, and used it for years. Around 2003 I lost it. Long story short I loaned it to someone and never got it back. Guessing you know the moral to that story.

Just recently I've gotten the urge to do some target shooting in my back yard - I can probably blame watching episodes of [[ASIN:B003NX6C1C Top Shot]] for that. So I wanted to replace my 1377, mainly because I still had all the accessories for it. So I got on Amazon and found this one to purchase.

To be honest, I did not read the information on the product page - just ordered it. A few days later I had the pistol in my hands. First thing I noticed is it's not quite the gun I remember having. Apparently the design has been changed. Gone was the pull knob that you used to cock the gun and instead there is a breach mechanism. I think I actually like the new design better.

One of the biggest surprise for me was that this model no longer makes use of Bbs. Gone is the magnetic tip on the end of loading pin. Wish I had know that before including this package in my order - [[ASIN:B000HKKY7M Crosman Copperhead 6000 Copper Coated BBs in a Bottle]]. But, that is my fault for not paying attention to what was on the product page.

Anyway - even just shooting pellets I am having fun with this gun. I also bought packs of these pellets - [[ASIN:B001DCB61Q Crosman Destroyer .177 Cal, 7.9 Grains, Pointed, 250ct]] & [[ASIN:B002DM0ZIU Crosman Hollow Point Pellets, 0.177-Calibre]]. Both seem to work well.

I've been having a lot of fun plinking cans and shooting targets. I think this pellet gun is great.
text_fidelity_b: Crosman American Classic Pump Air Pistol (.177)

I love fishing. There's nothing I'd rather do on the whole world. Nothing. You know what I mean... Lol! I've been fishing for decades, but have only been fly fishing for 3 years or so. I have several spinning rods in the $100-$200 range, and they are amazing. Unfortunately a $200 fly rod isn't the same as a $200 spinning rod. You can easily spend $3000 on a high end fly rod!

Well, I don't want to. I don't think it's necessary. But I've been fishing long enough that I can feel a great rod when I handle one. That's good, because I've seen lots of very expensive rods that were trash, and a few hidden gems that punched WAY above their weight. The Maxcatch Premiere line is one of those hidden gems. I picked this 3WT up just to check out, and after I effortlessly my fly 55' and landed it precisely where I wanted it. Over and over again. I mean it is so accurate that it's almost boring lol! And it's a $55 rod!

The blank is very sensitive, very light, very well finished and attractive, and the cork and dark chromed accents are beautiful. I'm surprised at how nice the cork is at this price point!

So I fish. A lot. I used to sell fishing equipment for a living, and I've handle a lot of gear. Is this Maxcatch a Loop or high end Sage? No. But it's also not $400-$900. However, I'd put this up against ANY Reddington, Fenwick, or lower end Sage any day and put money on the Maxcatch.

Get this rod. You'll be glad you did. You'll catch a ton of fish if you do your part, because this is a magnificent tool at an amazing price!

EDIT: I caught that monster 'Bow on the 4wt. Great fight! The rod was bent in half for 5 minutes, and held up great. And I felt every run, head shake, and dive. Great rods!

Schwinn Fitness 140 Upright Exercise Bike (Discontinued) Like many others, I researched this bike for about 2 weeks before deciding to purchase it. I read everything I could find about Schwinn bikes period. The model before this (the 130) is what I was going to purchase at WalMart, it was cheaper but I would have to pay for tax & shipping (free shipping and no tax on Amazon.com) so it was only going to save me about $30 at WalMart (for the older model) so I am definitely glad I decided to buy the 140 at Amazon.com.
The previous model (130) was highly rated/recommended on the Consumer Report websites and that made me realize that a newer model would/should be even better. I live in a small apartment and although I wanted the recumbent one, I had to go with the upright. Not to mention, I figured I could work on my posture while riding upright. (ha ha) This bike is just what I need to get in shape. I have a leg injury and I am overweight and out of shape. I needed a piece of equipment that I could commit to and not feel like I was doing a dreaded chore. I can hop on this bike and watch tv, listen to music, talk with people around me, or just look out of my window.

At first I felt like the price was expensive compared to the other models, but it's true, you get what you pay for. As I mentioned, I am overweight and I needed something that would last while I pursued my fitness goals. The other brands are not built as well as the Schwinn models. Simply look at the frame work and tubing and you can tell.
After I put it together (without any problems whatsosever) I realized that it was of good quality and worth the money I spent. The setup was easy. I am a female with manicured nails and I didn't even chip my polish putting this bike together. I also didn't require any help. It was really easy. I had my laptop on my sofa with the manual enlarged (I went to the Schwinn website and downloaded it) so that I could see the images clearly, but I mainly used the paper manual that the bike came with.

I read the instructions for the setup of the user profile and everything went just fine.
~I read some reviews about little issues with customizing, but if you just take your time and read the manual, you will really see its not difficult. When you set up a custom workout, you have to realize that it goes through 30 levels so it appears as though nothing is happening, but be patient as you customize it and you will see that it is working right.~
~Also the Heart Rate monitor, if you simply plug it in on the side, it should work just fine. You just have to look for the spot to plug it in to.~
I have only used the bike 4 times so I can't give you any long term use information, other than the programs are nice, the resistance is great, and it has a lot of features on the console once you set up your user profile, but I can say that this is a very good investment for anyone considering purchasing a quality exercise bike. It is a good piece of equipment. If you have to save up a little to get the bike, start saving! If you are considering a different brand, forget about it! If you think that its hard to put together, get over the thought! If you are worried about it not being right for you, try it and you will like it!

I have a lot of weight to lose and I don't like going to the gym. I walk around my neighborhood which is ok, but now I can get a good little cardio workout. I am so glad that I got this bike. I am helping myself in the long run. This is the best way to spend over $300 and have something well worth it!

No missing/broken pieces, no damaged stabilizers, no damaged or flimsy box. I ordered and received in exactly 7 days. ***I'm NOT discrediting anyone's reviews about problems they had with their purchase, I am just stating that my purchase was problem free***

~I will add another review/or update in the future about how the bike is performing~ I hope this helps motivate someone!
text_fidelity_b: Schwinn Fitness 140 Upright Exercise Bike (Discontinued)

text_fidelity_a:
Triple-Insulated Stainless-Steel Water Bottle Flip-Top Lid - (20 oz) Insulated Water Bottles, Keeps Hot and Cold - Wide Mouth and Leakproof - Canteen Water Bottle Great for Office, School, Biking Etc. My water bottle should:
1. Open easily with one hand
2. Keep the water cold
3. Be tough
4. Be easy to drink from
5. Be easy to clean.
6. (Extra credit) Be really easy to carry. Or not be bad at it.

I don't want to suck the water; I prefer to pour it into my mouth. So a tiny hole or straw is a no-go.

I had an Aladdin that was all that, but the spring eventually broke. Can't open one-handed anymore.

I bought a variety of water bottles to try out. This is my favorite. It's all of the above, with one caveat and one addition.

It opens easily, as long as there's no vacuum lock (i.e. you didn't put ice in and close it, resulting in the air inside cooling and forming suction.) The thermos is great. It's made of metal and heavy plastic.

IF you move the handle (the white ring) back BEFORE you open the bottle, it's easy to drink from. Otherwise the spout doesn't really come out far enough to get it close to your mouth. But that's easy to do.

Fully dishwasher safe. And very easy to carry, especially with that large handle/carry ring. Which is a solid loop. An example of this done badly is many of the UnderArmor bottles, which have a split ring for carrying that you really can't carry with a finger when full because the prongs of the split point in and dig into your finger.

The Extra Credit: There's a screen to prevent random ice bits from going into your mouth. It's removable, but I love this thing. I like my sports-water cold, but don't want to chew on ice during exercise.
text_fidelity_b: Triple-Insulated Stainless-Steel Water Bottle Flip-Top Lid - (20 oz) Insulated Water Bottles, Keeps Hot and Cold - Wide Mouth and Leakproof - Canteen Water Bottle Great for Office, School, Biking Etc.

text_fidelity_a: Trideer Padded Workout Gloves for Men - Gym Weight Lifting Gloves with Wrist Wrap Support, Full Palm Protection & Extra Grips for Weightlifting, Exercise, Cross Training, Fitness, Pull-up Gloves arrived just in time to head to the gym.  I bought these gloves for two reasons: (1) need the wrist support (2) don’t want calluses.  My wrists need the extra support from years of working as a barista (repetive motion injury is real).  The wrist support on these gloves felt great, but the actual glove fit felt too roomy.  My hand measured at 8.5 inches so I ordered the large according to the chart.  Long story short, these gloves will certainly help my wrists, but I fear I may end up with blisters due to the glove fit instead of the calluses that would result from not wearing gloves.  Not sure that’s a step in the right direction.  Contacted customer support and asked if I should have ordered mediums given my measurements.  They said to return the large gloves and order mediums.  Honestly, doesn’t seem worth the hassle and time for gloves that are just as likely to not fit well.  To sum up, they seem like decent gloves if they fit, which they don’t based on their own size chart.  If you don’t mind ill fitting gloves these are for you.

This cooler is incredibly well-made and I'm thrilled that I got it! (I ended up buying everyone their favorite team's cooler in this same brand, and they were a huge hit over the holidays!)

The first great surprise when it arrived was that it is made by Coleman, with tags on it to prove it. Coleman doesn't make bad stuff, in fact, they have a long history of well-made products, so that was a really nice bonus.

On top of that, there are all kinds of quality extras built into it. For example, when you lift the lid, there is a mesh ice-pack holder built right into the top of it. On the outside of it, there are mesh holders on each side (I use them for napkins, straws, or nutrition bars). Then in the front there is a nice zippered compartment that you can securely stash a few things in. The zippers are high quality and the materials, inside and out, are high quality as well. The strap is wide, strong and adjustable. Another nice perk is that it has a little pad where the strap will go over the shoulder, which really makes carrying it much more comfortable. The cooler holds a lot, and really does a great job at keeping things nice and cold. I just put my ice packs in it with our bottles, sandwiches, etc., and we are good to go.

I also got one of these coolers for a friend who is disabled and likes to keep a cooler next to her bed. Well, she'd gotten fed up with coolers that didn't keep things cold for very long and she had switched to using a spaghetti pot (for real!) with ice packs in it, to keep her ginger ale chilled, for constant nausea. She said that with a few frozen ice packs in it, she actually can go two whole days without having to replace the ice packs. She also said it fits great on her scooter when she's on the go.

Made by Coleman, like I said, and with lots of nice features, this high quality cooler is a must-have and a great gift. Check out the same cooler with other team logos. Igloo BMX 52 Quart Cooler with Cool Riser Technology I purchased the Igloo BMX Cooler to replace an Ozark Trail 25qt rotomolded cooler that I purchased from Wal-Mart before an impromptu camping trip. I was very disappointed with the OT cooler, it claimed to hold ice for 4.5 days but on day two of my trip over half the ice was melted. I had a family member coming out to visit and camp with me so I decided to order the 52qt version of the Igloo BMX. It was actually cheaper than the Wal-Mart cooler and twice the size.

We filled the Igloo up on a Sunday afternoon packed pretty full with food, beer and water. We were planning on a 3-day trip. I saved as much ice as I could at home and we bought one more bag on the way out of town. Day 1 after over 24 hours I opened the drain and only a tiny bit of water came out. Already much better performance. On Tuesday we moved campsites and got gas and added another bag of ice since we bought more food to replenish. Day 3 on Wednesday a fair amount of water drained from the cooler but it still had plenty of ice and was plenty cold. I had put 8 frozen water bottles inside and they were all frozen still.

I went to empty the cooler on Day 4, a full ~96 hours of use and there was still a lot of ice left in it. I have no doubt that you could make this last 5 days or even longer if you keep adding fresh ice every couple of days. If we didn't add the second bag, most of it would have probably melted by day 3/4.

At the time of this review I purchased the red/black 52qt cooler for $77. I'm impressed enough with it that I decided to order a 25qt one was well for solo trips and returned my Ozark Trail cooler. I will add another review or update this one after I use the 25qt cooler. But $140 for a nice rotomolded 52qt and 25qt cooler is less than half the price of ONE comparable Yeti. So glad I didn't buy into the hype.
text_fidelity_b: Igloo BMX 52 Quart Cooler with Cool Riser Technology

SUUNTO Movestick Mini (Black, One Size) worked with my Garmin 310XT on my Mac Pro without having to install anything. I already had the Garmin ANT+ stick installed and was using that, I simply took that out of the USB slot and put this in. I though I'd have to install something but after awhile the Garmin started syncing to it. Love that it worked right away. Although some times after a workout it takes a bit longer for it to recognize and connect automatically to my Garmin 310xt and start the data transfer. Usually I just leave the ANT+ stick in my Mac and synch my workouts after I'm done. However on a recent out of town trip I had forgotten to pack the ANT+ stick so I needed a replacement. I had read that this works just as well as the Garmin (some reviewers say even better) so at a significantly lower price and smaller size than the Garmin stick, I decided to give this a try so that I could keep it with my MacBook Pro that I use when traveling. I am very pleased with it and it is definitely worth it for the better price and works just as well as the Garmin stick, except for the occasional times when it doesn't seem to find the Garmin. When that happens I've just pulled it out and put it back in the USB slot and it usually finds the Garmin and starts transferring the data.

In Summary:

Pros:
+ Works great with Mac OSX - just plug it in!
+ cheaper than the Garmin ANT+ stick
+ small form factor - so no worry about accidentally bumping it against it and knocking it out of the USB slot during data transfer

Cons:
+ Some times takes a while to recognize my Garmin 310xt
+ small form factor - could get lost easily - but this is not really an issue to me, though may be for some folks so thought I'd mention it.

Conclusion: If it didnt' have that occasional little blip of not connecting, I'd give it 5 stars. Still I'm very pleased with it and would definitely recommend it!
text_fidelity_b: SUUNTO Movestick Mini (Black, One Size)

M MAXIMUMCATCH Maxcatch Extreme Graphite Fly Fishing Rod 4-Piece 9 Feet with IM7 Carbon Blank, Hard Chromed Guides, A Cork Grip（Size:3/4/5/6/7/8/10wt） (Extreme Rod, 9ft 4weight) Let's just say it. This is a darn nice rod. Is it a Sage? A Reddington? A Loop? Of course not. But it's also not $400.

I got this rod because I have 5wt and 6wt rods which were a bit more costly, but I wanted a 4wt for some smaller streams I'm going to be hitting. I won't spend much time there, and money is not abundant, so I figured I would try one of these. Boy was I surprised! I was expecting some moderate (slow) action rod, sloppy, and Heavy. This is light, crisp, and a joy to cast! The cork is great for this price point, and it's all put together and presented quite nicely.
There's an attitude in fly fishing that if it's not expensive, it's not worth using. Unfortunately we don't all have the ability or desire to spend $500 on a rod. For those of us in that situation, this is a magnificent option.

Look at it like this. You buy a rod at Scheels or Cabela's because you're getting a quality product at a slightly discounted price because it's store brand rather than big name brand. And that usually is the case and works well. Some of the best fishing gear I've got, and I've got a lot, was got from those brands I just named. These Maxcatch rods are built on the EXACT same blanks that the Scheel's Outfitter MDD fly rods are built on. And those were being sold for $100.

With that in mind, know that when you get one of these you aren't getting a Loomis rod. But this is probably the best sub-$120 fly rod you can get, and that leaves a lot of money for flies, tippet, line, and a reel.

I'll update this review with pics next time I go out. Buy one of these with confidence. I'll probably buy another for my wife and get a 3wt for me. I'm sold on this brand!
text_fidelity_b: M MAXIMUMCATCH Maxcatch Extreme Graphite Fly Fishing Rod 4-Piece 9 Feet with IM7 Carbon Blank, Hard Chromed Guides, A Cork Grip（Size:3/4/5/6/7/8/10wt） (Extreme Rod, 9ft 4weight)
